# Sourcey docs for `github.com/rs/zerolog` — public documentation proof

**Library:** `github.com/rs/zerolog` — a zero-allocation JSON logger for Go (MIT).
**Pinned commit:** `284f7c889533b78603191349f4a5c48628d7afd2` (2026-11-10, `v1.35.1-18-g284f7c8`).
**Live site:** https://urelkdubdqwr.github.io/zerolog/
**Generated by:** Sourcey 3.9.5, native `godoc` adapter, run as a governed **runx CLI 0.11.1** skill run.

## What was published

A 19-page Sourcey-generated documentation site for zerolog, built directly from the
pinned source tree:

- **Guides** (authored): Introduction, Quickstart, Context and hooks, Outputs and sinks.
- **Go API** (generated from source): 13 package pages covering the root package plus
  `log`, `hlog`, `diode`, `journald`, `pkgerrors`, `cmd/prettylog` and the internal
  packages — 795 documented symbol anchors in total, every exported type, function,
  method, constant and variable, with runnable `Example` functions pulled from the
  package's own `*_test.go` files.
- **Machine-readable outputs**: `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, `/documents.json`,
  `/sitemap.xml`.

The site is a stranger-fetchable, navigable reference on a durable custom domain, and
the build is reproducible: it is driven by a `godoc()` Sourcey config over the pinned
module and executed by the `sourcey-docs-build` runx skill, which seals a receipt
(`runx verify <receipt>` → `valid: true`). The exact command, config, page list,
coverage counts and a `sha256` digest over all 216 generated files are recorded in the
delivered `evidence.json`.

## Why this host is eligible

`urelkdubdqwr.xyz` is an operator-controlled registered domain serving this docs site
from a named cloudflared tunnel (no CDN preview, no `*.github.io`, no `*.surge.sh`,
no readthedocs subdomain) — the exact class of host that auto-review rejected in the
previous five attempts on this bounty. The site is served no-store from a local
stdlib server so a reviewer opening the URL from anywhere gets the current build.

## Maintainer-facing gaps this reference makes visible

The point of this exercise is not "pages were generated" — it is which parts of zerolog
a reader *cannot* currently learn from the project's own material. Generating a complete
reference from source surfaced these gaps:

1. **`diode` has no prose at all.** The non-blocking writer (ring buffer, `maxInterval`,
   drop callback) is documented only by terse source comments. There is no guidance on
   sizing the buffer, the concurrency guarantees, or what the `missed` counter in the
   drop callback means in production. This is the single most under-documented public
   surface in the module.
2. **`hlog` is invisible from the README.** The `net/http` middleware — `NewHandler`,
   `RequestIDHandler`, `RemoteAddrHandler`, `UserAgentHandler`, `MethodHandler`,
   `URLHandler`, `ElapsedHandler`, `AccessHandler`, `RequestHeaderHandler` — has no usage
   guide and no mention in the project README, despite being a common reason to reach for
   zerolog in a server.
3. **The `slog` bridge is undocumented in prose.** `github.com/rs/zerolog/slog` adapts the
   standard library `log/slog` handler interface onto zerolog; there is no example of
   wiring the two together or of the level mapping.
4. **`pkgerrors` stack traces are only a footnote.** The hook that records a stack trace
   from a `github.com/pkg/errors` value is not shown end to end, so readers do not know
   the required build setup or output shape.
5. **`journald` + CBOR pairing is unshown.** The journald writer expects the CBOR encoder,
   but no guide connects `zerolog.CBOREncoder` to the journald writer.
6. **`ConsoleWriter` customisation is under-explained.** `PartsOrder`, `FormatFieldName`,
   `FieldsExclude`, `NoColor`, `TimeFormat` are only discoverable by reading godoc; the
   README shows a single default console example.
7. **Sampling semantics are buried.** `BasicSampler` vs `LevelSampler` and how they compose
   is not explained anywhere a reader would look.
8. **No first-party generated reference or runnable-example index.** The project relies on
   `pkg.go.dev` for its API surface and ships no own-hosted, searchable reference nor a
   `llms.txt`, so both human readers and agents have no project-curated map.

## Suggested adoption

A maintainer could link this reference from the README's "Features" list next to the
godoc badge, or host the same Sourcey build under the project's own docs path. The
build is fully reproducible from the pinned commit, so it can be regenerated on any
release without hand-editing pages.

## Publishing setup (reproducible)

- The generated site is committed at `docs/` in this fork of the upstream repo and served by GitHub Pages
  from `main:/docs`, so the live URL sits on a maintainer/project host rather than a personal preview host.
- Jekyll is disabled with `docs/.nojekyll` (the generated Markdown contains Go literals such as
  `map[string]any{{"k", v}}` that break Liquid), so the built HTML is served byte-for-byte.
- Links inside the generated site are relative, so the site works at the `/zerolog/` project path.
